w.t:
CANCELLED ELECTRONIC NAVIGATIONAL CHART (ENC)
ADVISORY.
USERS OF NGA ENC PRODUCTS ARE ADVISED OF
POTENTIAL UNINTENDED ECDIS BEHAVIOR WHEN
PROCESSING CANCELLED CHARTS, INCLUDING
REINSTALLATION OF RECENTLY CANCELLED CHARTS ON
SOME SYSTEMS WITHOUT OBVIOUS ERROR OR
WARNING MESSAGES.
NGA HAS CONFIRMED THIS ISSUE AFFECTS NAVY VMS 9.5 AND
RAYTHEON ANSCHUTZ SYNAPSIS NX SYSTEMS. THIS ISSUE DOES NOT
AFFECT NAVY ECDIS. OTHER SYSTEMS ARE CURRENTLY UNASSESSED.
USERS MAY REFERENCE NGA'S ENC CATALOG (GLOBAL
OR REGIONAL PRODUCT LISTINGS) FOR A LIST OF
CANCELLED CHARTS WHICH SHOULD BE UNINSTALLED
FROM ECDIS.
NGA'S GLOBAL ENC CATALOG IS AVAILABLE ON
HTTPS://MCDP.NGA.MIL, WITH REGIONAL ENC PRODUCT
LISTING SPREADSHEETS CONTAINED WITHIN EACH
REGION'S ZIP ON ESYNC, NGA'S WEBSITES, AND
WORLDCOVER DVD.
USERS MAY FILTER PRODUCT LISTINGS FOR EDITION OF
CXL AND SORT BY ISSUE DATE TO SEE MOST RECENT
CANCELLATIONS.
CHARTS CANCELLED WITHIN THE LAST 90 DAYS ARE
ACTIVELY DISSEMINATED BY NGA AND MOST LIKELY
CANDIDATES FOR INADVERTENT REINSTALLATION.
NGA IS CONSULTING WITH THE USER COMMUNITY TO
ASSESS POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THE CANCELLED CHART
DISSEMINATION PROCESS TO MITIGATE THIS POTENTIAL
UNINTENDED ECDIS BEHAVIOR.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Arctic District (D17) LNM17-248B89
w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, TERRITORIAL SEA - SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA)
General / Hazards To Navigation / Obstructions
ConocoPhillips Alaska, Inc. (CPAI) plans to conduct marine ocean and seabed characterization studies near Oliktok Point. Studies will include buoy installation, tide gauge installation, bathymetric surveys, and navigational hazard surveys during the open water seasons of 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027. Temporary monitoring equipment will be placed in the area to support the studies. This request is specific to activities planned for the 2026 season; an LMN will be submitted in subsequent years as needed. Buoy installation includes the deployment and recovery of three wave buoys offshore of Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. Preliminary buoy locations are included in Table 1 and shown on the attached map; final buoy locations may vary by about 1 nautical mile from the preliminary locations based on planning with local vessel operators and conditions encountered in the field. Buoy 1 will be installed in shallow water, approximately 5 to 10 feet deep. Buoys 2 and 3 will be installed in deeper water, approximately 25 to 30 feet deep. All buoys will float on the surface. Final buoy locations, depths, and water depth will be recorded and submitted within two days of deployment. Each Spotter buoy will be moored to the seafloor and will have a spar buoy equipped with an LED strobe light to alert mariners. Buoys will be deployed in late-July or early- August and recovered in late-September to mid-October. One tide gauge will be installed at or near the Oliktok Point during the 2026 open water season. The tide gauge will consist of a pressure transducer located in a water depth of three to five feet, a cable to shore, and a data recorder onshore. The pressure transducer will be located about 20 feet from shore and will be mounted on a ¾ inch pipe that sticks up above the water approximately 3 feet. The pipe will be driven 2 to 3 feet into the seabed using a post drive and will be clearly marked for safety. The onshore data recorder will be kept in a weather resistant container (e.g. cooler or bucket) and secured to the gravel bag jetty on the west side of Oliktok Point. A survey staff will be installed next to the pressure transducer to provide manual readout. The staff will also be attached to a ¾ inch pipe driven into the seabed in the same manner as the pressure transducer. The tide gauge will be installed at the beginning of the open-water season. The tide gauge and associated materials will be removed prior to freeze up. The stake on which the tide gauge is mounted could present a hazard for small boats transiting near the beach. Mariners should reduce wake when transiting the area and maintain a distance of at least 100 feet from the stake in the water and the data recorder on shore. Work is planned to begin as early as July 10, 2026. Please contact Miranda Buckmaster at (907) 263-4868 or miranda.buckmaster@conocophillips.com should you have any questions or require additional information.
USCG Arctic District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.t:
SECTOR ANCHORAGE, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA) - PRINCE WILLIAM SOUND
General / Hazards To Navigation / Hazards
Location: 61-10.32N 148-28.50W 61-10.24N 148-03.45W 61-02.28N 148-03.45W 60-55.81N 148-28.99W 61-10.32N 148-28.50W The State of Alaka is issuing routine updates on the Barry Arm Landslide Tsunami risk. This threat is located in Barry Arm and has the potential to create a tsunami if/when a landslide is generated that impacts the water in Barry Arm. If/when this occurs localized wave heights will be very hazardous in Barry Arm and Harriman Fjord. Port Wells and Passage Canal will also see inundation and strong, unusual currents for hours following an event. The geologic makeup of the area is similar to Alaskan locations where two previous landslide caused tsunamis occurred, in Lituya Bay (1958) and Icy Bay (2015), both causing extremely large but localized tsunamis. Mariners should maintain vigilance when in the vicinity of Barry Arm or nearby waters and be prepared to depart the area if any unusual geologic activity is observed. Studies are being conducted and the situation is being monitored to allow for a better understanding of the potential results of a slide. Additional information is available at https://dggs.alaska.gov/hazards/barry-arm-landslide.html.
Valid 2024-10-28 to 2029-10-27.
USCG Arctic District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

The maintenance which began in September 2026, will continue to be conducted from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Monday-Friday; through March 31, 2027. A 40-foot work barge and a tugboat will continue to be located in and around the vicinity of the bridge. The project foreman can continue to be reached at (609) 579-8147. Mariners should use extreme caution navigating through the area. During the maintenance period, the bridge will be maintained in the closed-to-navigation position to perform structural steel repairs to the bridge bascule span. The bridge will not be able to open for emergencies. There is no immediate alternative route for vessels unable to pass through the bridge in the closed position. Location: 38-57.35N 074-52.45W Bridge Name: 621 County Route Bridge All interested parties are notified that the Commander, Coast Guard East District has received a proposal from the Cape May County Bridge Commission with plans for replacement of an existing highway drawbridge across a navigable waterway of the United States. WATERWAY AND LOCATION: Middle Thorofare, New Jersey Intracoastal Waterway (NJICW), at mile 112.2, at approximate location [38-57.35N 074-52.45W], and the Upper Thorofare, at mile 0.0, at approximate location [38-57.32N 074-52.62W] near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. CHARACTER OF WORK: The proposed project is to replace the Two-Mile drawbridge, located on County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, with a fixed bridge that will carry County Route 621 (Ocean Drive), across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare, near Lower Township, Cape May County, NJ. The purpose of the project is to address structural, geometric, carrying capacity, and operational deficiencies of the Cape May County Bridge Commission-owned bridge located across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, on the Ocean Drive Causeway, and to provide safe, efficient, and reliable passage for all modes of transportation. The existing drawbridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, has a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 23.00 feet above mean high water in the closed position and unlimited vertical clearance in the open position. The replacement bridge will be a fixed bridge across Middle Thorofare, NJICW, and Upper Thorofare. The portion of the replacement bridge across the Middle Thorofare, NJICW, will provide a horizontal clearance of 80.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 80.00 feet above mean high water. The portion of the replacement bridge across Upper Thorofare, will provide a horizontal clearance of 50.00 feet and a vertical clearance of 49.73 feet above mean high water. A copy of Preliminary Public Notice D05PPN-06-2026, which describes the proposal in detail, can be obtained by calling (571) 607-6762 or by viewing at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/public-notice-for-bridges-active (select East District). Comments will be received for the record at the address in the header or via email at (D5Portsmouth-BridgesPublicNotice@uscg.mil) no later than December 4, 2026.
Valid 2026-11-04 to 2026-12-05.

General/Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges)/Dredging Mariners are advised that The King Company, Inc. will be conducting hydraulic dredging operations in the Caseville Federal Channel, Michigan from September 21, 2026 through November 15, 2026. The dredge “Buxton II” will operate 24 hours per day, 7 days a week (weather permitting). Submerged dredge pipe will be lying on the lake floor and will be marked by orange round buoys every 1,000 feet. Two white buoys will be visible north and south of the dredge marking winch anchor locations. The dredge disposal area begins 13,728 feet west of the channel and extends an additional 3,350 feet westward. Material will be placed between the Ordinary High Water Mark (beach) and the 4-foot depth contour. The disposal area will be marked with white buoys on each corner. During rough seas, a bright yellow pipe pontoon measuring 25’ x 8’ x 6’ with two flashing amber lights on each end will be floating outside of the channel. A second identical bright yellow pipe pontoon with two flashing amber lights will be located in the disposal area. Mariners are requested to avoid the dredge, all pipelines, buoys, anchors, and pontoons, maintain a safe distance, reduce wake, and proceed with caution. The main point of contact is Superintendent Joseph Martin. For emergencies or questions, contact the main office at (616) 399-1784 or Superintendent Martin directly at (941) 628-6783.

Mobile Channel - Safety Zone/Naval Protection Zone --- On: 2026-11-11 --- The U.S. Coast Guard, State, and local law enforcement will enforce a Naval Protection Zone and a Safety Zone on navigable waters within the Captain of the Port Mobile area for the arrival of the M/V EX ENTERPRISE, expected on or about November 11, 2026, until the vessel is towed to its final mooring on the Mobile River. The Safety Zone will include all navigable waters within the Mobile Bar Channel, beginning at Mobile Bar Lighted Buoy 1 (LLNR-6100), northward through the boundaries of the Mobile River Channel, ending at the Cochrane Bridge. This zone will be enforced to prevent meeting situations with the M/V EX ENTERPRISE during the dead-ship tow. Portions of the Safety Zone intersecting the GIWW or other intersections with Federal Channels will be enforced to the extent necessary to prevent meeting situations during the transit and are not expected to be enforced after the M/V EX ENTERPRISE and all vessels involved in the towing operation clear the intersection. The Naval Protection Zone will include a 500-yard zone around the vessel and will be enforced from the vessel’s entry into the COTP Mobile Zone until the vessel is safely moored on the Mobile River. No person or vessel may enter or remain in the zone unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative. No vessel or person may enter within 100-yards without authorization. Vessels within 500-yards must operate at the minimum speed necessary to maintain a safe course. To seek permission to enter these zones, mariners can contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM Channel 16 during the enforcement period. Those authorized transit within the zones, must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. Concerned parties should contact the U. S. Coast Guard Sector Mobile Command Center at (251) 266-5888 or on VHF-FM Channel 16.

Texas City Channel - Monopile Operation ---  --- Monopile driving operations will be conducted along the Texas City Channel near Docks 42 and 43. Two configurations will be utilized by the monopile operation project vessels. 1. When the materials barge is utilized, the configuration will extend to the middle of the channel and will restrict vessel transits to tows with a single barge only. 2. When the materials barge is not part of the configuration, tows with two barges may transit. U.S. Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service Houston-Galveston will implement the following vessel traffic measures until further notice: • 7:00 a.m. - 10:00 a.m.: No ship traffic. Single barge tow transits only when materials barge is part of the monopile configuration. • 10:00 a.m. - 12:00 p.m.: Normal traffic pattern, no restrictions. • 12:00 p.m. - 4:00 p.m.: No ship traffic. Single barge tow transits only when materials barge is part of the monopile configuration. Tows are requested to coordinate at least 2-hours in advance to ensure the configuration of the operation can be determined to manage vessel transits. The M/V RUSSELL MARINE 1 will monitor VHF-FM Channels 13 and 87A, or can be contacted at (281) 979-4696 to coordinate towing vessel passing arrangements.
Valid 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-13.

w.t:
MOBILE CHANNEL - MOBILE RIVER
General / LAA / RNA / Safety Zone
Mobile River Channel - Safety Zone ---  To: May 2030 --- The Captain of the Port (COTP) Mobile is enforcing a fixed Safety Zone in accordance with 33 CFR 165.T08-1214 surrounding the M/V EX ENTERPRISE as the vessel is moored at a receiving facility located on the Mobile River at 701 South Royal Street, Mobile, AL. This Safety Zone is necessary to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from hazards associated with a dismantling operation, including removal of hazardous and regulated materials, and continuous work activity on and around the hull. All navigable waters of the Mobile River along the RDB will be designated as a fixed moored Safety Zone and will be bound by the following coordinates: 30-40.57N 088-02.27W, 30-40.57N 088-02.22W, 30-40.30N 088-02.08W, 30-40.32N 088-02.27W and north along the shoreline to the point of origin. The Safety Zone does not include waters within the Mobile River Federal Channel; therefore, no impact to commercial vessel traffic is anticipated. This zone will be enforced for the duration of dismantling operations, and remain in effect until the COTP determines the area no longer presents safety concerns. The dismantlement project is expected to progress to a safe stage approximately May 2030. In the event this fixed moored Safety Zone is no longer needed before May 2030, mariners will be notified through a Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) or other appropriate means. No person may enter or remain in the zone unless authorized by the COTP or a designated representative. Those in the Safety Zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP’s designated representative. To seek permission to enter, mariners can contact the COTP or the COTP’s representative on VHF-FM Channel 16.
Valid 2026-11-09 until further notice.

General / Miscellaneous
Alabama River - In accordance with Section 7-11 of the ACT Master Water Control Manual dated April 2022, full navigation channel availability on the Alabama River is dependent upon channel maintenance, seasonal flow conditions, and basin status. Flows for navigation are most needed in the unregulated portion of the lower Alabama River below Claiborne Lock and Dam. Alabama Power Company (APC) operates its reservoirs on the Coosa and Tallapoosa Rivers to provide a minimum navigation flow target in the Alabama River at Montgomery, Alabama. Basin status criteria are correlated to APC Drought Operations (ADROP) updates which monitors drought triggers related to basin inflow, state line flow on the Coosa River between Georgia and Alabama, as well as composite storage availability within the APC projects. These updates are provided monthly on the first and third Tuesday. Below is the most recent ADROP update provided by Alabama Power Company on October 20, 2026: *ADROP UPDATE* - Low Basin Inflow: FALSE - - Low State Line Flow: FALSE - - Low Composite Storage: FALSE - - Montgomery Flow Target: 4,200 cfs daily average (NOTE: ADROP requires one drought intensity level change per cycle regardless of the number of triggers enacted when exiting drought operations.) - - Current Operations: Drought Intensity Level 1 - Currently, based on profile survey conducted on 04JUN2024, a 10 ft tailwater elevation near Claiborne Lock is required to provide a 9 ft navigation channel on the lower Alabama River. A modified depth of 7.5 ft navigable draft can be provided with a tailwater elevation of 8.5 ft at the Claiborne Lock and Dam. Commercial mariners should check water levels daily and schedule lockage appointments by calling the Claiborne Lock Supervisor at (251) 282-4575. Tailwater elevations below Claiborne Lock and Dam can be viewed at: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-02428401
Position 31-36.90N 087-33.10W

General / MSIB
The U. S. Coast Guard COTP Pittsburgh has issued the following Safety Advisory due to inaccurate gauge readings on the Monongahela River. The lower gauge on John P. Murtha L/D, at Mile 42.0, has inaccurate readings and is in the process of being updated. Mariners are urged to exercise caution when transiting this area.

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Heartland District Rivers (D8) LNM08R-DD0837
w.t:
EMORY
General / Bridges / Repairs, Painting, Or Fender Replacement
Harvey H. Hannah Bridge; Commencing September 5, 2026, and continuing until December 1, 2026, Mid-State Construction Co., will be conducting bridge repairs. Vertical clearance may be reduced due to a containment/work platform below the bridge deck. Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m., 7-days a week. Dive crews will be conducting scow repairs on Pier 1 and 2 on the weekends. A dive boat will be on-scene monitoring VHF-FM Channels 13 and 16. Mariners are urged to exercise caution while transiting under the bridge.
Position 35-55.63N 084-33.10W
USCG Heartland (MRS) District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Heartland District Rivers (D8) LNM08R-CBBBEA
w.t:
LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER - UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER
General / MSIB
Mariners are advised to stay clear of the quoin on miter gate #4 on the upstream end of the I-Wall at L/D Nr. 3, in the vicinity of Mile 796.9. There is potential to contact exposed steel in the area. All tows transitioning the lock should avoid landing or rubbing on the portion of the I-Wall. Mariners may contact L/D Nr. 3 via VHF-FM Channel 14, or at (651) 290-5062, for additional information.
USCG Heartland (MRS) District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Heartland District Rivers (D8) LNM08R-75E94F
w.t:
LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER - OHIO RIVER
General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Facilities, Barriers, Manmade Reefs, Riprap, Jetties / Dikes
Continuing until March 31, 2027, Underwater Construction Corporation, dredging and mooring cell repairs are being conducted along the RDB, at the AEP Rockport Power Plant, in the vicinity of Mile 744.8. Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m., 7-days a week. The contractors floating plant will consist of one crane barge and one material barge. Mariners are requested to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize their wake and proceed with caution.
USCG Heartland (MRS) District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Heartland District Rivers (D8) LNM08R-FD46FB
w.t:
LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER - UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER
General / Bridges / Repairs, Painting, Or Fender Replacement
I-57 Bridge: Commencing June 29, 2026 and continuing through November 30, 2026, bridge cleaning and painting operations will take place on the I-57 Bridge, Mile 7.5. Daily work will occur Monday through Saturday, from 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Rigging and containment under the bridge will reduce the vertical clearance by 3 feet. Mariners should transit the bridge with caution and immediately report any unsafe conditions to the U.S. Coast Guard.
Position 37-01.47N 089-12.65W
USCG Heartland (MRS) District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

General / MSIB
Location: 41-16.93N 072-54.93W SUMMARY: The U.S. Anny Corps of Engineers (USACE). New England District, will be conducting dredging operations in support of the New Haven Harbor Improvement Project in New Haven, Connecticut. Mariners are advised to use caution, maintain a proper lookout. and communicate early with the dredging vessel when operating in or near the project area. SITUATION: The New Haven Harbor Improvement Project will modernize approximately 5.5 miles of the federal navigation channel serving the deep-water terminals of New Haven. Great Lakes Dock and Dredge Company, under contract with USACE, is expected to conduct work over two dredging cycles. The first one beginning in October 2026 and continuing through March 2027, and the second cycle beginning in October 2027 and continuing through March 2028. Operations are planned to take place 24 hours a clay, 7 days a week. Planned improvements include deepening the entrance channel, main channel, maneuvering area, and turning basin from 35 feet to 40 feet; widening the entrance channel from 500 feet to 600 feet outside the breakwaters; widening the channel bend between the breakwaters from 560 feet to 800 feet; widening the main channel inside the harbor from 400 feet to 500 feet; and optimizing the turning basin for larger vessels. Dredging operations may affect normal vessel movement, maneuvering, and transit within New Haven Harbor. Mariners should anticipate the presence of dredging equipment and associated support vessels within the federal navigation channel and surrounding work areas. Vessels looking to transit the area are urged to contact the dredge early to arrange safe passage and to maintain a proper lookout when navigating near operations. COMMUNICATIONS: For urgent safety-of-life matters, please contact the Sector Long Island Sound Command Center on VHF-FM Channel 16 or call (866) 299-8031. Working Vessels will monitor channels 13, 16, and 79. Additionally, please check USCG Navigation Center oflen for updates to the public from the US Coast Guard. Questions regarding this bulletin may be directed to Lieutenant Joel Chapman. ChiefofWaterways Management Division at (475) 355-5336 or email SECLlSSPWMarineEvent@uscg.mil.
Valid 2026-10-26 to 2027-04-01.

General / Bridges / Temp Deviation
WASHINGTON – LAKE WASHINGTON SHIP CANAL – Montlake Bridge deviation notice The Coast Guard intends to approve a temporary deviation from the normal operating schedule that governs the Montlake Street Bridge (BRDG UID 31183) across the Lake Washington Ship Canal, mile 5.2. The Montlake Street Bridge need not open the draw for marine vessels during heavy road traffic for the 2026 University of Washington football games on the following dates and times: - 06 Sep 1000 to 1330 and 1600 to 1830; - 12 Sep, 0930 to 1300 and 1530 to 1800; - 19 Sep, 1300 to 1700 and 1900 to 2200; - 26 Sep, 1700 to 2030 and 2300 to 0130; - 09 Oct, 1500 to 1830 and 2100 to 2330; - 07 Nov, 0930 to 1300 and 1530 to 1800; - 21 Nov, TBD. The deviation is necessary to accommodate vehicular traffic attending football games at Husky Stadium at the University of Washington, in Seattle, Washington. This deviation will allow Montlake Bridge to remain in the closed-to-navigation position before and after each game. Due to television scheduling, game times will be published at later dates when determined, and the MSI will be updated with the bridge closure times. Vessels which do not require a bridge opening may continue to transit beneath this bridge during the closure. The bridge will be required to open, if needed, for vessels engaged in emergency response operations during this closure period. The Coast Guard will publish any updates or changes to this operating schedule in future MSI announcements. The bridge shall operate in accordance with 33 CFR § 117.897 at all other times. If any mariner cannot support the dates listed for a bridge closure, please submit a comment by 04 Jul 2026 at SMB-CGD-NW-BRIDGES@USCG.MIL. For more information, contact Colleen Kelly at (425) 739-3700.

SECTOR COLUMBIA RIVER, TERRITORIAL SEA - SECTOR COLUMBIA RIVER, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA)
General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Boring and Core Samples
TYPE OF WORK: Marine dive operations at each of six lat-lon coordinates, corresponding to the horizontal directional drill (HDD) exit points of six (6) subterranean conduits for the future housing of up to six buried fiber-optic telecommunications cables. The HDD equipment staging and drilling operations will take place from a single onshore location in Grays Harbor County. Marine activity will be limited to dive operations. LOCATION WHERE WORK WILL BE DONE: Outer Pacific coast of Washington State south of Westport, Grays Harbor County, at six points approximately 0.75 nautical miles offshore Cohassett Beach. LAT/LONG OF MARINE OPERATIONS: (Degrees, Minutes, Seconds – Coordinates in WGS84) Position 1. N46 52 28.3607; W124 08 22.0226 Position 2. N46 52 26.7419; W124 08 22.0186 Position 3. N46 52 25.1255; W124 08 21.8943 Position 4. N46 52 23.5069; W124 08 21.8440 Position 5. N46 52 21.8924; W124 08 21.6716 Position 6. N46 52 20.2860; W124 08 21.3807 CHART NUMBERS: US4WA1EE; US3WA1DE BEGINNING/ENDING DATES: October 15 2026 – February 15 2027 HOURS OF OPERATION: Daylight hours only. Dive operations to be conducted approximately 12 days total during the operational period between October 15 2026 – February 15 2027. EQUIPMENT ON SCENE: Dive support vessel R/V Zephyr with anchor spread. RADIO FREQUENCY VESSEL CAN BE CONTACTED ON: Monitoring VHF Channels 16 and 19. PASSING ARRANGEMENTS/SAFE NAVIGATION DISTANCE: Mariners are requested to keep a minimum ½ nautical mile distance from the dive vessel. To ensure diver safety, any trolled, drift or fixed gear such as pots/traps is requested to remain clear of the dive vessel by a distance of ½ nautical mile. w.id: US Coast Guard LNM Northwest District (D13) LNM13-662DDC
w.t:
SALMONBAY
General / Bridges
WASHINGTON – LAKE WASHINGTON SHIP CANAL – SHILSHOLE BAY – Bridge notice (Revised) Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway Company (BNSF) will be performing heavy rail maintenance/construction on the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge (BRDG UID 31177) (AKA BNSF Bridge 6.3), mile 0.1, across the Lake Washington Ship Canal in Seattle, Washington. The construction work requires the draw of the subject bridge to be closed from 02 November 2026 to 25 November 2026. This draw closure corresponds with the USACE’s large Hiram M. Chittenden Lock closure. The Coast Guard has approved a temporary deviation to the operating schedule that governs the Salmon Bay Railroad Bridge from 0600 on 02 November 2026 to 1600 on 25 November 2026. The draw will be able to open from 8 A.M. to 8 P.M on 14 - 18 November 2026, if a 24-hour notice is given to the bridge operator. The subject bridge provides 43 feet of vertical clearance in the closed-to-navigation position at mean higher high water. Vessels which do not require a bridge opening may continue to transit beneath the bridge during this closure period. This construction requires barges in the navigation channel during the same time as USACE’s annual lock closure and maintenance to minimize impacts. A crane and material barge will be positioned in the water to service the work of erecting temporary trusses that are required to execute the counterweight change out. During this timeframe, access on the southern channel to the small locks will be in operation during the large lock closure. A construction zone will be established for mariners to navigate around at minimum safe speed. The subject bridge will not be able to open for emergencies, and there is no immediate alternate route for vessels to pass. For more information on this draw bridge closure contact Travis Woodley at travis.woodley@bnsf.com or (682) 978-3311.
Position 47-40.02N 122-24.13W
USCG Northwest District Local Notice to Mariners 45/2026

w.t:

General / Miscellaneous
PacWave continues to maintain a network of site monitoring equipment, seafloor instrumentation, and subsea cable infrastructure throughout the PacWave South wave energy test site, approximately 7 nautical miles WSW of the Yaquina Bay Entrance. Some of the monitoring buoys are low profile and may be difficult to see in elevated sea states. All buoys have a yellow hull, are lighted with a flashing amber light, and are deployed as single-point moorings. PacWave has also installed four long-term surface marker buoys that visually delineate the corners of the test site: NW (44°34.9988'N, 124°14.4998'W), NE (44°35.0465'N, 124°13.1008'W), SE (44°33.0437'N, 124°12.9700'W), and SW (44°33.0000'N, 124°14.3730'W). These corner markers are approximately 9 feet tall, have a yellow / red hull, a fixed yellow tower structure with integrated radar reflector, green grating on the lower half of the tower, reflective tape on the upper tower, and are lighted. These markers are also single-point moorings and will remain in place as part of PacWave’s maintained offshore infrastructure. Mariners should be aware that subsurface equipment and mooring components may also be present. Mariners are requested to avoid the test site if possible and to use caution when navigating in or near the area. For additional information, contact brett.hembrough@oregonstate.edu or 541-737-9023. If there is an emergency or concerns regarding this equipment, please call our 24 / 7 Watch Desk at 541-819-4096.

w.t:

General / Miscellaneous
MSIB 004-26 Quiet Sound Voluntary Slowdown https://www.pacificarea.uscg.mil/Our-Organization/Northwest-District/District-Staff/dp/dpw/notices/ The Quiet Sound voluntary commercial vessel slowdown in Admiralty Inlet aims to reduce underwater noise in Southern Resident killer whale critical habitat. The 2025-26 slowdown will be in effect starting at 0001 PST on 3 September 2026 and will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PST on 31 January 2027, at the latest, depending on orca presence. More information can be found at: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown. When in effect, the slowdown requests all inbound and outbound commercial vessels transiting through the slowdown zone not exceed the following speeds through water when safe and operationally feasible: 11 knots – General cargo, bulkers and tankers 14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels The voluntary vessel slowdown takes place in the inbound and outbound lanes of the shipping lanes within these boundaries: Northwest: a line drawn from Pt Hudson (48-07.04N 122-44.93W) to Admiralty Head (48-09.25N 122-40.77W) Northeast: a line drawn from Randall Pt (47-58.99N 122-21.17W) to Mukilteo Light (47-56.89N 122-18.48W) South: a line drawn from Apple Cove Pt (47-48-55.926N, 122-28.51.186W) to Edwards Pt (47-48.20N 122-23.70W) Speed transition zones are in place about 5 nautical miles prior to entering the slowdown area. Any directions from Puget Sound Vessel Traffic Service take precedence and supersede these measures. The voluntary slowdown is led by the Quiet Sound program at Maritime Blue, in cooperation with government agencies, tribal governments, industry partners and conservation groups. For more detailed information related to this slowdown and the Quiet Sound program, including a graphic of the voluntary slowdown area, refer to the following web address: https://quietsound.org/admiralty-inlet-slowdown.

SECTOR HONOLULU, TERRITORIAL SEA - KAUAI ISLAND
General / Naval Activity / Naval Gunnery Exercises
Intermittent missile firing operations are conducted by the Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF), Barking Sands, Kauai, in the Whiskey 188 (W-188) operating area. Operations are conducted periodically throughout each week in an area bound by the following coordinates: 22:00N/159:51W, 22:00N/160:00W, 22:04N/160:06W, 21:59.5N/160:21W, 22:05N/161:35W, 22:45N/161:25W, 22:56N/161:49W, 23:34N/161:18.6W, 23:57N/160:41W, 25:41N/161:36W, 26:00N/159:58W, 25:47N/158:15W, 23:54N/158:15W, 22:20N/159:09W, 22:21N/159:30W, 22:13N/159:42W, 22:00N/159:51W Intermittent high power radar operations are conducted by PMRF at the following position: 22:03N/159:47W Request all mariners remain at least one mile off the coastline between Kokole Point and Nohili Point. Vessels may be requested to alter course due to firing operations and are requested to contact "Pacific Missile Range Facility" on VHF-Ch 16 prior to entering the above boundaries. If unable to contact the PMRF prior to entering or while in the warning area, relay messages through U.S. Coast Guard Honolulu. Vessels inbound and outbound for Hawaiian ports will create the least interference to firing operations as well as enhance vessel's safety by passing South of the Islands of Kauai and Niihau during the specified times. Federal law provides for civil penalties of $40,000 and/or criminal penalties of 6 years in prison for each violation of the PMRF safety zone during the schedule of designated activity (33CFR 165.1406). The following are hazardous operations to mariners for November 9th, 2026 through November 18th, 2026: 09 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 10 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 11 NOV 0630-1800 KAULAKAHI CHANNEL AND NOHILI POINT OUT TO 60NM WEST THROUGHT NORTH. 12 NOV 0630-1800 KAULAKAHI CHANNEL AND NOHILI POINT OUT TO 60 NM WEST THROUGH NORTH. 13 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 14 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 15 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 16 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 17 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED. 18 NOV NO HAZARDOUS OPERATIONS SCHEDULED.

General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Dredging
General/Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges)/Dredging 27918 Great Lakes Dredge and Dock Company, LLC will begin mobilizing for a dredge project on or about September 22, 2025. Vessels and equipment being used are DREDGE 54 (Mechanical Clamshell Dredge), DREDGE NEW YORK (Backhoe Bucket Dredge),Tug BERING DAWN, Tug AMY E. HEBERT, Tug LARRY J. HEBERT and Tug LIZ ALMA, SURVEY BOAT PEARL RIVER, CREW BOAT COOPER RIVER, Scows GL501, GL502, GL701, GL702. Vessels will be monitoring VHF-FM channels 07 and 12/16 The purpose of the Port Everglades Sand Bypass project is to create infrastructure on the north side of the Port Everglades Inlet in Broward County, Florida. Work to be completed under this contract consists of dredging a sand trap and a portion of the rubble spoil shoal and disposal of the dredge material in the Port Everglades Harbor Ocean Dredged Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredging operations are anticipated to commence on October 22, 2025, and will take place 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. With an estimated completion date of July 18, 2027. The DREDGE 54, along with DREDGE NEW YORK which will start on or about December 18, 2025, are planned to collectively dredge more than 400,000 CY of material from the north side of the Port Everglades entrance channel, immediately seaward of the north jetty and beach north of the inlet. The dredges would appreciate slow bell passing. While approaching the jetty dredging work area location. The material will be placed into scows and towed to the Port Everglades Harbor ODMDS, which is located approximately 3.1 nautical miles northeast of the entrance to Port Everglades Channel, outside of State Waters. There is a project tow route between Red Buoy 2 and the ODMDS CenterPoint. Fishermen and trawlers should be aware of limited mobility for tug and scow transits. Small-Vessel Captains should take caution to avoid passing between the scow and towing tug while under transit. While not always visible at a distance, there is a large steel-tow cable that passes between the bow of the scow and the stern of the towing tug. The survey vessel, Pearl River, will conduct survey operations of the ODMDS disposal area and work area corridors (during daylight hours/7 days per week). A crew transfer vessel, the Cooper River, will transfer crew between the shoreside boarding location at Bahia Mar Yachting Center and the dredging equipment. w.t:
SECTOR SAN FRANCISCO, TERRITORIAL SEA - SECTOR SAN FRANCISCO, SUBMERGED LAND ACT (SLA)
General / Autonomous Vessel Operations
The Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) will be conducting autonomous, unmanned maritime vehicle operations using two Liquid Robotics, Inc. Wave Gliders in Monterey Bay. The scope of operations includes continuous scientific ocean data collection utilizing Wave Gliders remotely attended from MBARI. Operations are scheduled to take place 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from January 12, 2026, through December 31, 2026. Wave Glider vehicles will be deployed in the vicinity of Moss Landing and will operate continuously between latitudes 36.30000° N and 37.20000° N, extending shoreward from as far west as -122.97650° W. Each Wave Glider is approximately 8 feet by 2 feet (surfboard size), yellow/copper in color, with a contact plaque and a mast extending 1 meter above the water surface supporting a flag. The vehicles are wave-powered, carry no fuel, lubricants, or hydrocarbons, move at speeds of approximately 1 knot, and are designed to give way or part if encountered by a vessel. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution. For further information, please contact MBARI at 831-775-1700 or waveglider@listserver.mbari.org, or Liquid Robotics 24/7 WGOC Operations at 888-574-4574 or +1 408-636-4205.

GOLDEN GATE BRIDGE - SAN FRANCISCO BAY
General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Dredging
The Sevenson Environmental Services and PGE will be conducting environmental dredging and installing steel piles from 19 May, 2026 - 30 November, 2026. Operation times will be five to six days per week, with hours of operations 5am to 7pm(local). This operation will include the use the following vessels and equipment: 40x80 PC650-01, 40x80 PC650-02, Crane Barge MICHEAL LIND, Staging barge STELLA LIND, Tug CASSIE LIND, Tug ARCHIE LIND, SEVENSON 01 and 02 work boats. The project location is centered at approximately at the San Francisco Pier 41 to Pier 43, in position: 37°48'35.20"N; 122°24'46.41"W. All vessels and equipment on site will monitor VHF-FM Channels 13, 14 and operating on 11. Sevenson will utilize two 40x80 barges with PC650 excavators on them to perform environmental dredging and capping via clam shell bucket and conventional buckets. Sevenson has hired Lind marine to subcontract out work including the transloading operations via E-Crane “Greta Jean Lind”. The Michael Lind (Crane Barge) will be in the area for support, along with another spud barge “Stella Lind” for staging room. Steel pipe pile will be installed roughly up to 400 ft offshore to hold the turbidity curtain. During the project, we will also install 504 wooden piles for slope stability. The PC650 will load into 6x – 100CY (30’ x 40’) scows and pushed to the edge of the curtain. From there the E-Crane will take the material and transload into large Jumbo Hoppers. Lind Marine will use the Cassie Lind (1200 HP tug) to push the scows up to Birds Landing, CA to an offload facility. At the offload facility there will be an E-Crane to offload the material from the scows onto land. Lind Marine will use the Cassie Lind (1200 HP tug) to push the scows up to Birds Landing, CA to an offload facility. At the offload facility there will be an E-Crane to offload the material from the scows onto land. Lind Marine will also use the Cassie Lind to push scows to Redwood City, CA to an offload facility. All mariners are advised to use caution when transiting the area. For further comments or details, please contact SEVENSON ENVIROMENTAL project manager at (716) 807-1937. Alternate contacts: Jake Wood (607) 794-1654 and Terry Templeton (716) 476-6790.

The Dutra Group and Camenzind Dredging, Inc., under contract with the City of Stockton, will conduct maintenance dredging within Buckley Cove, Stockton, California, including marina slips, fairways, and the boat-launch area, with placement at the Roberts Island Dredged Material Placement Site (DMPS), located across the San Joaquin River from Buckley Cove. Floating/submerged pipeline will be marked with 30-inch diameter spherical yellow floats; anchors will be marked with 30-inch diameter spherical white buoys. Lighted “Danger” buoys with reflective tape and radar reflectors will be used where the dredge pipeline poses a navigational hazard. Mariners are advised to use extreme caution when transiting the area. General / Miscellaneous
The Coastal Data Information Program (CDIP) has deployed a moored wave buoy, CDIP ID 94 (Cape Mendocino, CA), NDBC WMO ID 46213, on June 3, 2026. The buoy is located at 40-17.49N 124-44.85W, approximately 17.5 nautical miles southwest of Cape Mendocino, at a depth of 346.0 meters. The buoy is a Datawell Directional Waverider 4 model and measures waves, sea surface temperature, air temperature, and surface current speed and direction. The new position is within 500 yards of the previous position. The buoy is described as a 3-foot diameter sphere with an attached telemetry whip antenna and a nighttime yellow warning flashing light. The light sequence consists of 5 flashes at 1-second intervals, with a period of 20 seconds between each series, and a visual range of one kilometer. The buoy is painted yellow and marked "Wave Buoy," with the URL cdip.ucsd.edu and phone number 858-534-3032. All mariners are advised to transit the area with caution.

General / Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges) / Facilities, Barriers, Manmade Reefs, Riprap, Jetties / Dikes
Contractors for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will conduct marine operations for levee rehabilitation along the Sacramento River between River Miles 47.3 and 53.5 . Waterside work is scheduled to begin July 6, 2026, and will continue through approximately November 30, 2026. Operations will involve up to three crane barges (including Crane Barge #12, measuring approximately 140' x 50'), a tugboat, two workboats, and a rotation of flat deck barges. Flat deck barges will transit between the job site and the San Rafael Rock Quarry, utilizing pre-existing moorings along the Sacramento River, including locations at River Miles 26 and 27 near Walnut Grove, CA. At the end of each shift, barges will be spudded in place and marked with steady burning white lights on all corners. Mariners are advised to use extreme caution, transit at their slowest safe speed to minimize wake, and maintain a safe distance. Project vessels will monitor VHF-FM channels 9, 16, and 68A, and can be contacted directly at (707) 333-5029.

NORTHERN CALIFORNIA-OAKLAND INNER HARBOR-FRUITVALE AVE RAIL BRIDGE-The lift span of the rail bridge is kept in the partially opened position providing 80 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water. The lift span can be raised to its fully open position upon request to the drawtender at the Miller Sweeny (Fruitvale Ave) bridge. The following is the new navigation lighting configuration at the rail bridge. 1. When the bascule span of the highway bridge is in the closed-to-navigation position and the lift span of the railroad bridge is in the partially open position, providing 80 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, the lift span center channel navigation lights will show a red 180-degree center span light on the upstream and downstream lower edge of the span. 2. When the bascule span of the highway bridge is in the fully opened position and the lift span of the railroad bridge is in the partially opened position, providing 80 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, the lift span center channel navigation lights will show one solid 360-degree green light and one flashing 360-green light on the upstream and downstream lower edge of the span, providing a range for the centerline of the channel between both highway and railroad bridges. 3. When the bascule span of the highway bridge is in the fully opened position and the lift span of the railroad bridge is in the fully opened position, providing 135 feet of vertical clearance at mean high water, the lift span center channel navigation lights will show two solid 360-degree green lights on the upstream and downstream lower edge of the span, providing a range for the centerline of the channel between both highway and railroad bridges.
